title: Claims Desk Guidance: Refusal at Handover and Transport Damage on Delivery & Pickup Appointments
content:
At the handover of a Delivery & Pickup Appointment, the buyer may refuse the vehicle. What the refusal does to the purchase order and the delivery fee depends on whether the condition report supports it. New damage found after the vehicle has been accepted is handled under the transport damage rule.

## Refusal at handover

**For cause.** A refusal is for cause when the condition report records one of the fulfillment method's accepted refusal reasons. Odometer variance counts only when the variance exceeds the purchase program's handover odometer tolerance. In that case the purchase order is cancelled as vehicle-unavailable, and every delivery fee is refunded.

**Without cause.** Any other refusal cancels the purchase order as customer-cancelled. The delivery fee is refunded only when the method's refusal-without-cause switch is on.

When the buyer refuses, the appointment's status moves from dispatched to refused, and the date of refusal is recorded as its closing date.

### Input, judgement and outcome

| Condition report records | Judgement | Purchase order | Delivery fee |
|---|---|---|---|
| New cosmetic damage | For cause | Cancelled as vehicle-unavailable | Every delivery fee refunded |
| New mechanical issue | For cause | Cancelled as vehicle-unavailable | Every delivery fee refunded |
| Odometer variance above the purchase program's handover odometer tolerance | For cause | Cancelled as vehicle-unavailable | Every delivery fee refunded |
| Odometer variance not above that tolerance | Without cause | Cancelled as customer-cancelled | Refunded only if the method's refusal-without-cause switch is on |
| None of the accepted reasons | Without cause | Cancelled as customer-cancelled | Refunded only if the method's refusal-without-cause switch is on |

**Hypothetical odometer cases.** Where a purchase program's handover tolerance is 200 miles:
- A recorded variance of 260 miles exceeds the tolerance, so the refusal is for cause.
- A variance of 150 miles does not exceed it. A refusal on that basis is without cause.
- A variance of exactly 200 miles does not exceed the tolerance either.

## Transport damage after handover

New damage noticed after handover is transport damage when it is reported within the method's damage report window hours after handover. Kestrel then repairs it at no cost to the buyer, up to the method's transport damage repair cap. Above that cap, the buyer's remedy is the 7-day return. A condition finding reported in this way is recorded with the repair estimate.

**Hypothetical repair cases** (a method with a 48-hour window and a $750.00 cap; damage reported 20 hours after handover, so within the window):
- Repair estimate $430.00: within the cap. Kestrel repairs the damage at no cost to the buyer.
- Repair estimate $1,180.00: above the cap. The buyer's remedy is the 7-day return.
